pmc-11423378.title: Risk of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) Among 18 to 48 Month Old Children: A Multi-Center Study in Qatar
pmc-11423378.creator: Aisha Abdulraheem Sameea, Ekram Wassim Abd El-Wahab, Sherif Omar Osman
pmc-11423378.description: Background. Little is known about autism spectrum disorder (ASD) in Qatar. The lack of consensus in ASD screening has led to differences in the reported prevalence with escalating rates over time. Objective(s). To screen for ASD and to identify associate factors among Qatary children aged 18 to 48 months. Methods.

pmc-11430741.title: Ferroptosis in Renal Cancer Therapy: A Narrative Review of Drug Candidates
pmc-11430741.creator: Lingyan Yu, Yuyueyang Qiu, Xiangmin Tong, Claudia M Kowolik
pmc-11430741.description: Simple SummaryTreatment options for patients with advanced renal cancer are limited, as one of the main methods, chemotherapy, is prone to drug resistance in the course of treatment. There have been numerous studies confirming that ferroptosis is involved in the development of renal cancer and drug resistance during treatment.

pmc-11505395.title: Uptake of Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances in Mixed Forages on Biosolid-Amended Farm Fields
pmc-11505395.creator: Thomas L Simones, Chris Evans, Caleb P Goossen, Richard Kersbergen, Ellen B Mallory, Susan Genualdi, Wendy Young, Andrew E Smith
pmc-11505395.description: Models to predict perfluorooctanesulfonic acid (PFOS) concentrations in livestock based on soil concentrations are essential to guide decisions surrounding food testing and farm management. A key parameter in modeling soil-to-livestock exposure pathways is the plant transfer factor (TF) from soil into forages.

pmc-11622111.title: Caregiver burden among informal caregivers of stroke survivors in Harare, Zimbabwe
pmc-11622111.creator: Farayi Kaseke, Lovemore Gwanzura, Timothy Kaseke, Cuthbert Musarurwa, Elizabeth Gori, Tawanda Nyengerai, Aimee Stewart
pmc-11622111.description: BackgroundStroke presents significant challenges for both survivors and caregivers, particularly in resource-limited settings like Zimbabwe. Identifying factors contributing to caregiver burden strain (CBS) is crucial to enhance support strategies.ObjectivesThis longitudinal study identified caregiver and stroke survivor characteristics associated with CBS among caregivers in Harare, Zimbabwe.

pmc-11677096.title: The Molecular Mechanism Regulating Flavonoid Production in Rhododendron chrysanthum Pall. Against UV-B Damage Is Mediated by RcTRP5
pmc-11677096.creator: Fushuai Gong, Jinhao Meng, Hongwei Xu, Xiaofu Zhou, Pedro Martínez-Gómez
pmc-11677096.description: Elevated levels of reactive oxygen species (ROS) are caused by ultraviolet B radiation (UV-B) stress. In response, plants strengthen their cell membranes, impeding photosynthesis. Additionally, UV-B stress initiates oxidative stress within the antioxidant defense system and alters secondary metabolism, particularly by increasing the quantity of UV-absorbing compounds such as flavonoids.

pmc-12773513.title: Abstract 201: Feasibility of an 088” Catheter in the M1 segment for Mechanical Thrombectomy
pmc-12773513.creator: Muhammad W Khan, Benjamen M Meyer, Jessica K Campos, Fahad Laghari, David A Zarrin, Jonathan C Collard de Beaufort, Gizal Amin, Kiarash Golshani, Narlin Beaty, Matthew T Bender, Geoffrey P Colby, Li‐Mei Lin, Alexander L Coon
pmc-12773513.description: IntroductionPlacement of 088” aspiration catheters in the internal carotid artery (ICA) for aspiration in mechanical thrombectomy (MT) has been previously described. However, the use and safety of 088” aspiration catheters beyond the ICA has not been established. Here, we report the utilization and early safety outcomes of 088” catheter placement in the M1 segment for MT.

pmc-12971391.title: Variations in Seed and Fruit Traits of the Rare and Endangered Chinese Plant Lilium tsingtauense Along Environmental Gradients
pmc-12971391.creator: Wanpei Lu, Anning Ding, Xiao Guo, Pulin Sun, Xinqiang Jiang, Jinming Yang, Hai Wang, Xuebin Song, Qingchao Liu
pmc-12971391.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Lilium tsingtauense Gilg is a rare and endangered wild plant, but there is insufficient research on the environmental drivers of intraspecific variation in its seed and fruit traits. To investigate the responses of variations in seed and fruit traits to geographical and soil factors across different habitats, 37 sample plots were selected for investigation and statistics within an elevation range of 200–1000 m in Laoshan, China.

pmc-13128507.title: Advances in T-Lymphokine-activated Killer Cell-originated Protein Kinase Research in Cancer Over the Past Thirty Years
pmc-13128507.creator: Mengyu Zhao, Ran Zhao, Zigang Dong, Mee-Hyun Lee
pmc-13128507.description: Nearly thirty years ago, T-lymphokine-activated killer (T-LAK) cell-originated protein kinase (TOPK), also known as PDZ-binding kinase, was first identified as a serine/threonine kinase with limited known functions. Over time, this molecule has gradually revealed a far more striking role in cancer biology.

pmc-13296015.title: Genetic Determinants of Telomere Length and Their Role in Human Disease: Molecular Mechanisms and Underrepresented Populations’ Perspectives
pmc-13296015.creator: Viviana A. Ruiz-Pozo, Santiago Cadena-Ullauri, Rafael Tamayo-Trujillo, Patricia Guevara-Ramírez, Elius Paz-Cruz, Alejandro Cabrera-Andrade, Ana Karina Zambrano
pmc-13296015.description: Telomere length (TL) is a key determinant of cellular aging and genomic stability, influenced by genetic, molecular, and environmental factors. Progressive telomere shortening has been associated with degenerative and cardiovascular diseases, whereas longer telomeres have been linked to an increased risk of cancer, highlighting a dual and context-dependent relationship between TL and disease susceptibility.

pmc-13687615.title: Building Teacher Capacity for Inclusive Practice With Autistic Pupils: A Mixed-Methods Study of Self-Efficacy, Training, Attitudes, and School Context
pmc-13687615.creator: Anna Cook, Alice Boddy
pmc-13687615.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Autistic pupils in mainstream secondary schools often experience unmet needs, yet limited research has examined the combined influence of multiple theoretically relevant predictors of teachers’ self-efficacy and intentions to implement inclusive practice for autistic pupils. This mixed-methods study surveyed 126 staff from six secondary schools, assessing autism-specific training, perceived inclusiveness of the school environment, experience with autistic pupils, neurodiversity-affirming attitudes, personal connection to autism, and staff role.
